{{Short description|American molecular biologist}}
'''John J. Medina''' is a developmental molecular biologist with special research interests in the isolation and characterization of genes involved in human brain development and the genetics of psychiatric disorders. Medina has spent most of his professional life as an analytical research consultant, working primarily in the biotechnology and pharmaceutical industries on research issues related to mental health.

He was founding director of the [[Talaris Research Institute]], which supports [[researchers]] such as [[Patricia Kuhl]]<ref>UW News [http://uwnews.org/article.asp?articleID=1932  New $35.5 million Center for Mind, Brain and Learning created at UW] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100613120125/http://uwnews.org/article.asp?articleID=1932 |date=2010-06-13 }}. Accessed online 30 May 2009.</ref> and [[John Gottman]].<ref>Kitsap Sun [http://web.kitsapsun.com/brainchild/178058.shtml  Washington fertile ground for brain research] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090406165828/http://web.kitsapsun.com/brainchild/178058.shtml |date=2009-04-06 }}. Accessed online 30 May 2009.</ref> He directed Talaris until 2006, and now is the director of the Brain Center for Applied Learning Research at [[Seattle Pacific University]], which has worked on creating learning environments at [[Woodland Park Zoo]].<ref>Seattle Pacific Response. [http://www.spu.edu/depts/uc/response/autumn2k6/features/brainfriendly.asp Creating Brain-Friendly Spaces ]. Accessed online 30 May 2009.</ref> He is also an affiliate professor of bioengineering at the [[University of Washington School of Medicine]].

Medina wrote the column "Molecules of the Mind" for ''[[Psychiatric Times]]''.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20130202105621/http://www.psychiatrictimes.com/molecules Molecules of the Mind] (archived), ''[[Psychiatric Times]]''</ref>

==Education==
Medina earned his [[Ph.D.]] in [[molecular biology]] from [[Washington State University]] and is a national faculty fellow of [[Continuing Medical Education]], Inc., of Irvine, CA. In 2004, he was appointed to the rank of affiliate scholar at the National Academy of Engineering.<ref>Center for the Advancement of Scholarship on Engineering Education Affiliated Scholars [http://www.nae.edu/?ID=11797 Affiliated Scholars] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110610213218/http://www.nae.edu/?ID=11797 |date=2011-06-10 }}. Accessed online 18 May 2009.</ref>
